title: Filters, Blend Modes, Clipping, and Masks
summary: Change how an element looks or which parts remain visible.
nestedConcepts: Blend with content behind an element
Clip an element to a shape

subtopics.title: Apply visual filters
subtopics.explanation: The CSS `filter` property applies effects such as blur, brightness, grayscale, or drop shadow to the rendered element. For example, grayscale can de-emphasize a disabled thumbnail. Filters affect the whole rendered result and can create a stacking context, so test how they interact with overlays and performance.

subtopics.title: Blend with content behind an element
subtopics.explanation: `mix-blend-mode` combines an element’s colors with the pixels behind it. It can create image-overlay effects, but the result depends on the backdrop and may change when the layout changes. Use it sparingly, check text contrast, and set an isolation boundary when blending should stay within one component.

subtopics.title: Clip an element to a shape
subtopics.explanation: `clip-path` defines which part of an element remains visible, using a shape or path. For example, a circle clip can turn a square image into a circular avatar. Clipping changes appearance, not the underlying content or hit-testing assumptions; keep essential text and controls usable outside decorative effects.

subtopics.title: Use masks for gradual visibility
subtopics.explanation: A mask controls visibility using the transparency or brightness of another image. A gradient mask can fade an image at its edge, unlike a hard geometric clip. The element still occupies its layout space, and mask support can vary, so provide a sensible unmasked presentation.

subtopics.title: Check accessibility and rendering cost
subtopics.explanation: Filters, blending, clipping, and masks can reduce contrast or add rendering work. Preview effects on lower-powered devices and at different zoom levels. Keep important labels readable, and provide a plain fallback when the effect fails or makes content difficult to perceive.

foundations.overview: Filters adjust visual effects such as blur or brightness. Blend modes mix colors with what is behind an element. clip-path cuts content to a shape, while masks use transparency to reveal parts. These effects can cost rendering time and may reduce contrast.
foundations.mentalModel: They work like photo editing tools applied to a layer.
foundations.whyItMatters: They create visual treatments without needing a separate image for every variation.

keyTakeaways: mix-blend-mode combines colors with the backdrop.
clip-path defines a visible geometric region.
Masks use alpha or luminance to control visibility.
Check contrast and performance on real devices.

codeLab.instructions: Use clip-path to shape the color panel and keep the heading readable.
